\chapter{Grandparents, Aunts and Uncles}
\label{ch:ta-grandparents}
\hlchaptermodality{101}

\begin{chapteropening}
\textbf{By the end of this chapter:} \emph{I can name grandparents, an uncle and an aunt, and my father's younger brother.}

Complete the last lesson of chapter 101: i can name grandparents, an uncle and an aunt, and my father's younger brother.

\section[tāttā]{\ta{தாத்தா} (tāttā) — a grandfather}

\label{lesson:TA-C101-grandfather}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a wife, then the Tamil for a relative.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{தாத்தா}}
\textbf{\ta{தாத்தா}} (\emph{tāttā}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandfather\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{என்} \ta{தாத்தா}} — \textquotedblleft{}my grandfather\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
A grandfather.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāttā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{tāttā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉ tāttā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a wife, then the Tamil for a relative, then say \emph{tāttā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{தாத்தா} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A grandfather\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[pāṭṭi]{\ta{பாட்டி} (pāṭṭi) — a grandmother}

\label{lesson:TA-C101-grandmother}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a relative, then the Tamil for a grandfather.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{பாட்டி}}
\textbf{\ta{பாட்டி}} (\emph{pāṭṭi}) — \textquotedblleft{}grandmother\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{பாட்டி} \ta{வீடு}} — \textquotedblleft{}grandmother's house\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Both grandparents.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāṭṭi}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{pāṭṭi}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉ tāttā, eṉ pāṭṭi}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a relative, then the Tamil for a grandfather, then say \emph{pāṭṭi} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{பாட்டி} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A grandmother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[māmā]{\ta{மாமா} (māmā) — uncle, the mother's brother}

\label{lesson:TA-C101-uncle}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a grandfather, then the Tamil for a grandmother.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{மாமா}}
\textbf{\ta{மாமா}} (\emph{māmā}) — \textquotedblleft{}uncle\textquotedblright{}, above all your mother's brother; also \textquotedblleft{}father-in-law\textquotedblright{}.

Tamil kinship names the side of the family, not only the generation.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An uncle, named by side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māmā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{māmā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉ māmā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a grandfather, then the Tamil for a grandmother, then say \emph{māmā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{மாமா} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Uncle, the mother's brother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[attai]{\ta{அத்தை} (attai) — aunt, the father's sister}

\label{lesson:TA-C101-aunt}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for a grandmother, then the Tamil for an uncle.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{அத்தை}}
\textbf{\ta{அத்தை}} (\emph{attai}) — \textquotedblleft{}aunt\textquotedblright{}, your father's sister; also \textquotedblleft{}mother-in-law\textquotedblright{}.

\textbf{\ta{மாமா}} and \textbf{\ta{அத்தை}} pair up across the two sides of the family.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
An aunt, named by side.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{attai}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{attai}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉ attai}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for a grandmother, then the Tamil for an uncle, then say \emph{attai} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{அத்தை} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Aunt, the father's sister\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[cittappā]{\ta{சித்தப்பா} (cittappā) — the father's younger brother}

\label{lesson:TA-C101-fathersyoungerbrother}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Tamil for an uncle, then the Tamil for an aunt.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ta{சித்தப்பா}}
\textbf{\ta{சித்தப்பா}} (\emph{cittappā}) — your father's younger brother.

It ends in \textbf{\ta{அப்பா}}, \textquotedblleft{}father\textquotedblright{}: he is the \emph{little father}.

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
Grandparents, uncle, aunt, and a little father.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cittappā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{cittappā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} say \emph{eṉ cittappā}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Tamil for an uncle, then the Tamil for an aunt, then say \emph{cittappā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ta{சித்தப்பா} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}The father's younger brother\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
